newsitem.title: USA: American Air in pact to buy Shuttle.
newsitem.headline: American Air in pact to buy Shuttle.

text.p: American Airlines said Thursday it agreed to purchase Shuttle Inc., the successor to the Trump Shuttle, which is currently managed and partially owned by US Airways Group Inc.
American, a unit of AMR Corp, said it will purchase the stock, warrants and debt of Shuttle Inc. for an undisclosed price.
The former Trump Shuttle was taken over in April 1992 by a group of lenders. US Airways operates the shuttle under a management contract and holds 47 percent of the equity.
The Shuttle operates between New York and both Boston and Washington, one of the nation's busiest travel corridors.
American said the deal is contingent upon US Airways' decision not to exercise its option to purchase the Shuttle or its right to match American's offer.
In April, US Airways started to assess the value of the Shuttle, but made no decision whether to buy the commuter service.
US Airways' exclusive right to buy the Shuttle ended April 9, but the airline has the right to match any purchase offer made by another party over the next five years.
US Airways could not be immediately reached for comment.
